source_text:
Ἀλλὰ πάντα σοφῶς, καθὼς προεῖπον, πραγματευόμενος πρὸς λυσιτέλειαν ἔλεγεν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις· Ἀποκυλίσατε τὸν λίθον, ὅπως ἐξ αὐτῆς τῆς
νεκροφόρου ἀποφορᾶς μάθωσιν ὅτι ἐσάπη καὶ οὐκ ἐκλάπη. Ἀποκυλίσατε τὸν λίθον. 2 Τῶν δὲ ἀποκυλισάντων μετὰ γογγυσμοῦ– ἐδρίμυττεν γὰρ αὐτοὺς ἡ νεκροφόρος δυσήνιος ἀποφορά–, ἀποκυλισάντων δὲ τῶν παρόντων τὸν λίθον, εὐθέως ἐβόησεν ὁ κύριος λέγων· Λάζαρε δεῦρο ἔξω. ∆εσπότης ὁ καλῶν, οὐδεὶς ὁ ἀντιλέγων. Λάζαρε, δεῦρο ἔξω· πληροφόρησον Μάρθαν τὴν ἀδελφήν σου ὡς κελεύω καὶ οὐχ ἱκετεύω. Λάζαρε, δεῦρο ἔξω. Πρὸ τοῦ κατέλθω, ἔξελθε· ἐν σοὶ τὸν ἀρραβῶνα, ἐν ἐμοὶ δὲ τὸ τέλειον. Λάζαρε, δεῦρο ἔξω. Σὺ δὲ ἀκούων, ὦ φίλε, Λάζαρε, δεῦρο ἔξω, μὴ οἴου τὸν κύριον πολλὰς φωνὰς βεβληκέναι. Ἅπαξ ἐλάλησε καὶ ὃν ἔπλασεν ἤγειρεν· οὔτε γὰρ ὡς Ἠλίας ἔκλαυσεν οὔτε ὡς Ἐλισσαῖος ἠπόρησε. Μονοφθόγγῳ φωνῇ διύπνισε τὸν παρ' αὐτῷ καθεύδοντα εἰπών· Λάζαρε, δεῦρο ἔξω. Εἷς ὁ λόγος καὶ διάφορα τὰ θαύματα. Μόνον ὁ κύριος ἐφώνησε· Λάζαρε, δεῦρο ἔξω, καὶ εὐθέως αἱ σάρκες ἀπεπληροῦντο, αἱ τρίχες ἀντεφυτεύοντο, αἱ ἁρμονίαι συνεδεσ μοῦντο, αἱ φλέβες καθαρῷ αἵματι ἀντεγεμίζοντο. Ὁ ᾅδης κάτωθεν κοπτόμενος τὸν Λάζαρον προέπεμπεν. Ἡ ψυχὴ Λαζάρου παρακρατουμένη καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων παρακαλουμένη τὸ ἴδιον εἰς τὸ ἴδιον μετεχωνεύετο. Καὶ τὸ πάντων ἐνδοξότερον ἦν ὅτι πανταχόθεν δεδεμένος ἦν τοὺς πόδας καὶ τὴν ὄψιν κηρίαις καὶ ἀνεμποδίστως ἐβάδιζεν. ∆ιὸ καὶ ὁ κύριος δραστικώτερον πρὸς τοὺς παρόντας ὄχλους παρεκελεύετο λέγων· Λύσατε αὐτὸν καὶ ἄφετε ὑπάγειν. Βλέπε τὴν τοῦ κυρίου πραγματείαν καὶ πῶς τὰ πάντα σοφῶς οἰκονομεῖ. Πρὸς πληροφορίαν τῶν παρόντων ἔλεγε· Λύσατε αὐτὸν καὶ ἄφετε ὑπάγειν· ὡς τὸν λίθον ἀπεκυλίσατε καὶ τὸν τάφον ὑπεδείξατε καὶ τῆς ὀσφρήσεως μετήσχετε, καὶ τὰ νεκροτάφια λύσατε· τὸ μὲν ὡς εὐλογίαν τηροῦντες, τὸ δὲ ὡς μάρτυρες φυλάττοντες. Ἐὰν ἀπιστήσωσιν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ φαρισαῖοι ὡς οὐκ ἀνέστη Λάζαρος, δείξατε τὰ νεκροτάφια· ἐμφανίσατε τὰ σουδάρια ὡς ὁ παράλυτος τὸν κράβαττον. Ἡμεῖς δὲ τὰ βαΐα τῶν φοινίκων βαστάζοντες εἴπωμεν· Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις· εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου. Αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος σὺν τῷ παναγίῳ καὶ ζωοποιῷ πνεύματι νῦν καὶ ἀεὶ καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν. 3
thought_title: The strategy of the raising and the proof of the wrappings
orientation: Amphilochius is closing the homily by showing how Jesus' command to roll away the stone and then to unbind Lazarus was a deliberate strategy to make the onlookers witnesses of the raising, and he ends by calling the congregation to join the palm-bearing acclamation.
pass_a_gloss: But [he] all things wisely, just as I said before, arranging as strategy for benefit, was saying to the Jews: Roll away the stone, so that from the very corpse-bearing stench they might learn that he had decayed and was not stolen. Roll away the stone. And when those who rolled away [did so] with grumbling – for the corpse-bearing, hard-to-control stench was stinging them –, and when those present had rolled away the stone, immediately the Lord cried out, saying: Lazarus, come out. [He is] the Master who calls; no one [is] the one who speaks against. Lazarus, come out; fully convince Martha your sister that I command and do not beg. Lazarus, come out. Before I go down, come out; in you [is] the pledge, but in me the perfect [thing]. Lazarus, come out. But you, when you hear, O friend, 'Lazarus, come out,' do not suppose that the Lord cast many voices. Once he spoke and the one whom he formed he raised; for neither as Elijah did he weep nor as Elisha was he at a loss. With a single-sound voice he woke the one sleeping beside him, saying: Lazarus, come out. One [was] the word and various [were] the wonders. Only the Lord called out: Lazarus, come out, and immediately the flesh was being filled out, the hair was being planted again, the joints were being bound together, the veins were being filled again with pure blood. Hades below, being struck, was sending Lazarus forth. The soul of Lazarus, held fast and comforted by the holy angels, was being changed over from its own [place] to its own [body]. And the most glorious [thing] of all was that he was bound on every side, the feet and the face, with burial cloths, and he was walking without hindrance. Therefore also the Lord more vigorously to the crowds present was urging, saying: Loose him and let [him] go. See the strategy of the Lord and how he arranges all things wisely. For the full assurance of those present he was saying: Loose him and let [him] go; as you rolled away the stone and showed the tomb and partook of the smell, also loose the burial wrappings; the one [part] as a blessing keeping, the other [part] as witnesses guarding. If the chief priests and the Pharisees disbelieve that Lazarus rose, show the burial wrappings; display the burial cloths as the paralytic [displayed] the mat. But we, carrying the palm branches of the date palms, let us say: Hosanna in the highest; blessed [is] the one who comes in the name of the Lord. To him [be] the glory and the might with the all-holy and life-giving Spirit now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'strategy' for πραγματεία; the participle here is the verbal form of that same root, so 'arranging as strategy' keeps the connection to the fixed term.
The phrase is emphatic and repeated; 'corpse-bearing' preserves the compound adjective and 'stench' renders the odor carried off from the corpse.
The verb is an imperative to Martha and carries the sense of complete assurance, matching the later noun πληροφορία rendered 'full assurance.'
The glossary fixes 'pledge' for ἀρραβών, and the contrast with 'the perfect thing' requires the down-payment sense.
The glossary fixes 'burial wrappings' for νεκροτάφια, and the passage distinguishes them from the σουδάρια rendered 'burial cloths.'

choices.english: palm branches of the date palms
choices.why: The phrase is specific: βαΐα are the palm branches and φοίνικες the date palms, so the full phrase is rendered literally.

bible_refs.note: Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις· εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου

pass_b_english: But as I said before, he was arranging everything wisely, as I said before, as strategy for advantage when he said to the Jews: "Roll away the stone," so that from the corpse-bearing stench itself they might learn that he had decayed and was not stolen. "Roll away the stone."

When those present rolled away the stone with grumbling—for the hard-to-control corpse-bearing stench was stinging them—immediately the Lord cried out: "Lazarus, come out (John 11:43)." The Master is the one calling; no one speaks against him. "Lazarus, come out; fully convince Martha your sister that I command and do not beg. Lazarus, come out. Before I go down, come out; in you is the pledge, but in me is the perfect thing. Lazarus, come out."

But you, friend, when you hear "Lazarus, come out," do not suppose that the Lord shouted many times. He spoke once and raised the one he had formed. For he did not weep as Elijah did, nor was he at a loss as Elisha was. With a single-sound voice he woke the one sleeping in his presence, saying: "Lazarus, come out." One word, and the wonders were various. The Lord only called out, "Lazarus, come out," and immediately the flesh was being filled out, the hair was being restored, the joints were being bound together, the veins were being refilled with pure blood. Hades, cut off from below, was sending Lazarus onward. The soul of Lazarus, being detained and comforted by the holy angels, was being remolded, the soul into its own body. And the most glorious thing of all was that he was bound everywhere, his feet and his face with burial bands, and he walked without hindrance.

Therefore the Lord also commanded the crowds present more effectively, saying: "Untie him and let him go." See the Lord's strategy and how he arranges everything wisely. For the full assurance of those present he said: "Untie him and let him go. As you rolled away the stone and showed the tomb and shared in the smell, untie the burial wrappings too; preserve the stone as a blessing, keep the burial wrappings as witnesses. If the chief priests and the Pharisees disbelieve that Lazarus has risen, show the burial wrappings; display the burial cloths as the paralytic carried his mat."

But let us, carrying the palm branches of the date palms, say: "Hosanna in the highest; blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord." To him be glory and power with the all-holy and life-giving Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.

problems.quote: The soul of Lazarus, held fast and comforted by the holy angels, was being poured back, its own into its own.
problems.source_quote: Ἡ ψυχὴ Λαζάρου παρακρατουμένη καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων παρακαλουμένη τὸ ἴδιον εἰς τὸ ἴδιον μετεχωνεύετο.
problems.why: English garbles the sense; the Greek says the soul was being retained, comforted by angels, and transferred to its own place.
problems.fix: The soul of Lazarus, being retained and comforted by the holy angels, was being transferred back to its own place.

problems.quote: Hosanna in the highest; blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord (Matthew 21:9).
problems.source_quote: Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις· εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου.
problems.why: Matthew 21:9 does not contain ‘Hosanna in the highest’; the phrase belongs to Revelation 19:6.
problems.fix: Hosanna in the highest; blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord (Revelation 19:6).

problems.quote: corpse-bearing stench
problems.why: ἀποφορά means 'emanation/effluence,' not 'stench' specifically; 'corpse-bearing emanation' or 'corpse-bearing discharge' is the sense. 'Stench' over-specifies as smell.
problems.fix: corpse-bearing effluence

problems.quote: its own into its own
problems.why: The Greek idiom means 'its own [self/soul] into its own [body],' i.e., the soul returning to its proper place in the body. 'Its own into its own' is opaque and misses the soul-body referents.
problems.fix: its own self into its own body
problems.ruling: τὸ ἴδιον εἰς τὸ ἴδιον lacks referents; translation omits soul‑body sense

problems.quote: burial cloths
problems.why: κηρῖαι (honeycombs/wax cells) refers to the burial wrappings/coils, not 'burial cloths' generally. The glossary has 'burial wrappings' for νεκροτάφια and 'burial cloth' for σουδάρια; κηρῖαι are specifically the wax-like burial bands.
problems.fix: with the burial bands
problems.ruling: κηρῖαι are wax‑like burial bands, not generic 'burial cloths'

problems.quote: poured back
problems.why: μεταχωνεύομαι means 'was being melted down and recast,' 'refounded,' 'remolded'—metallurgical imagery of smelting. 'Poured back' loses the technical sense of reconstitution.
problems.fix: was being remolded
problems.ruling: μετεχωνεύετο = melted and refashioned, not merely 'poured back'

problems.quote: held fast
problems.why: παρακρατέομαι means 'was being detained/held back/restrained' (by Hades/angels), not merely 'held fast.' The soul is being kept from returning, then encouraged back.
problems.fix: being detained
problems.ruling: παρακρατουμένη = restrained/kept back, not simply 'held fast'

problems.quote: more forcefully
problems.why: δραστικώτερον means 'more effectively,' 'more actively,' 'with more efficacy'—not 'more forcefully' in tone. Jesus' command is strategically effective, not harsh.
problems.fix: more effectively

problems.quote: keep the one as a blessing, guard the other as witnesses
problems.source_quote: τὸ μὲν ὡς εὐλογίαν τηροῦντες, τὸ δὲ ὡς μάρτυρες φυλάττοντες
problems.why: The antecedents are confused. τὸ μέν...τὸ δέ refers to the two items: the stone (or tomb-opening act) as blessing, the burial wrappings as witnesses. 'The one...the other' is unclear; 'blessing' for εὐλογία is weak (means 'gift,' 'boon').
problems.fix: the former as a gift preserving, the latter as witnesses keeping
problems.ruling: τὸ μὲν… τὸ δὲ refer to stone and wrappings; English 'the one… the other' vague

problems.quote: do not suppose that the Lord uttered many voices
problems.source_quote: μὴ οἴου τὸν κύριον πολλὰς φωνὰς βεβληκέναι
problems.why: βεβληκέναι means 'had thrown/cast,' not 'uttered.' The idiom is 'threw many voices' = 'shouted many times/vociferously.' 'Uttered' is too neutral.
problems.fix: do not suppose the Lord shouted many times

problems.quote: the one sleeping beside him
problems.why: παρ' αὐτῷ means 'with him' (i.e., with the Lord), but 'beside him' is spatial; more importantly, 'sleeping' for καθεύδοντα misses the euphemism for death. The context is Lazarus dead, not literally sleeping beside Jesus.
problems.fix: the one who lay dead with him
problems.ruling: καθεύδοντα = euphemism for dead; 'sleeping' misrepresents death

problems.quote: Hades below, struck with grief, was sending Lazarus on his way.
problems.source_quote: Ὁ ᾅδης κάτωθεν κοπτόμενος τὸν Λάζαρον προέπεμπεν.
problems.why: κοπτόμενος means ‘being cut off’, not ‘struck with grief’.
problems.fix: Hades, cut off from below, was sending Lazarus onward.
problems.ruling: κοπτόμενος from κόπτω means 'cut, beat, mourn'; 'struck with grief' stretches to misleading.

problems.quote: Untie him and let him go (John 11:44).
problems.why: The source gives no citation; John 11:44 concerns removing the stone, not this command.
problems.fix: Untie him and let him go.
problems.ruling: Source has no citation; John 11:44 is 'Lazarus, come out' and removal of stone, not 'untie him'.

edits.new: The soul of Lazarus, being detained and comforted by the holy angels, was being remolded, its own self into its own body.

fixed: The soul of Lazarus: παρακρατουμένη means 'being detained/held back,' not 'held fast'; μετεχωνεύετο is metallurgical 'was being remolded/recast,' not 'poured back'; τὸ ἴδιον εἰς τὸ ἴδιον refers to the soul returning to its own body.
Hosanna in the highest: Matthew 21:9 lacks 'Hosanna in the highest'; the phrase is from Revelation 19:6.
corpse-bearing stench: ἀποφορά means 'emanation/effluence,' not specifically 'stench.'
burial cloths: κηρῖαι are the wax-like burial bands, not general burial cloths.
more forcefully: δραστικώτερον means 'more effectively/actively,' not 'more forcefully' in tone.
keep the one as a blessing, guard the other as witnesses: τὸ μέν...τὸ δέ refers to the stone/tomb-opening as gift and the burial wrappings as witnesses; εὐλογία means 'gift/boon,' not 'blessing.'
uttered many voices: βεβληκέναι means 'had thrown/cast,' idiom for shouting many times, not neutral 'uttered.'
the one sleeping beside him: καθεύδοντα is a euphemism for death; παρ' αὐτῷ means 'with him,' not spatial 'beside him.'
Hades below, struck with grief: κοπτόμενος means 'being cut off,' not 'struck with grief.'
Untie him and let him go (John 11:44): The source gives no citation; John 11:44 concerns removing the stone, not this command.

problems.quote: Hosanna in the highest; blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord (Revelation 19:6)
problems.source_quote: Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις· εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου
problems.why: Adds a Revelation citation not present in the source
problems.fix: Hosanna in the highest; blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord

problems.quote: cut off from below
problems.why: κοπτόμενος means 'beating (the breast), mourning, lamenting' not 'cut off'; Hades is personified as grieving/reluctantly releasing Lazarus, not being 'cut off'.
problems.fix: Hades, mourning from below, was sending Lazarus onward
problems.ruling: κάτωθεν κοπτόμενος = ‘from below, being cut’; context suggests lament, not literal ‘cut off’, altering Hades’ portrayal.

problems.quote: its own self into its own body
problems.source_quote: τὸ ἴδιον εἰς τὸ ἴδιον μετεχωνεύετο
problems.why: τὸ ἴδιον εἰς τὸ ἴδιον means 'its own (soul) into its own (body)'—the soul is being remelted/remolded back into its proper body, not 'its own self into its own body' which is tautological and obscures the soul-body reunion.
problems.fix: was being remolded, its own into its own
problems.ruling: τὸ ἴδιον εἰς τὸ ἴδιον μετεχωνεύετο = ‘its own into its own was remelted’; omission of ‘soul’ loses key meaning.

edits.old: Hosanna in the highest; blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord (Revelation 19:6).
edits.new: Hosanna in the highest; blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.

edits.old: Hades, cut off from below, was sending Lazarus onward.
edits.new: Hades, mourning from below, was sending Lazarus onward.

edits.old: was being remolded, its own self into its own body.
edits.new: was being remolded, its own into its own.

fixed: Removed the Revelation citation; the source has no scripture reference for the Hosanna acclamation.
Changed 'cut off' to 'mourning' for κοπτόμενος, which means beating the breast or lamenting, not being cut off.
Changed 'its own self into its own body' to 'its own into its own' to reflect the soul-body reunion without the tautology.

problems.quote: Hades, mourning from below
problems.why: Greek describes Hades as cutting off from below, not mourning.
problems.fix: Hades, cutting off from below

problems.quote: he was arranging everything wisely as strategy for their benefit
problems.source_quote: Ἀλλὰ πάντα σοφῶς, καθὼς προεῖπον, πραγματευόμενος πρὸς λυσιτέλειαν ἔλεγεν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις
problems.why: πρὸς λυσιτέλειαν means 'for advantage/profit,' not 'for their benefit'—whose benefit is ambiguous; the strategy serves Jesus' purpose of producing witnesses.
problems.fix: he was arranging everything wisely, as I said before, as strategy for advantage when he said to the Jews
problems.ruling: πρὸς λυσιτέλειαν implies advantage, not specifically ‘their’ benefit

problems.quote: the one who lay dead with him
problems.why: παρ' αὐτῷ means 'with him' in sense of 'in his presence/under his authority,' not 'dead with him'; καθεύδοντα is 'sleeping,' euphemism for dead.
problems.fix: the one sleeping in his presence
problems.ruling: τὸν παρ' αὐτῷ καθεύδοντα means ‘lying dead in his presence’, not ‘dead with him’

problems.quote: its own into its own
problems.source_quote: τὸ ἴδιον εἰς τὸ ἴδιον μετεχωνεύετο
problems.why: τὸ ἴδιον εἰς τὸ ἴδιον means 'its own [self] into its own [body]'; the soul is remelted/refashioned into its proper place, not 'its own into its own.'
problems.fix: was being remolded, the soul into its own body
problems.ruling: τὸ ἴδιον εἰς τὸ ἴδιον is garbled as ‘its own into its own’, loses meaning

problems.quote: preserve the former as a gift, keep the latter as witnesses
problems.source_quote: τὸ μὲν ὡς εὐλογίαν τηροῦντες, τὸ δὲ ὡς μάρτυρες φυλάττοντες
problems.why: τὸ μὲν...τὸ δὲ refers to 'the stone' and 'the burial wrappings' respectively, but the English reverses or obscures which is which; 'former/latter' order is unclear.
problems.fix: the stone as a blessing, the burial wrappings as witnesses
problems.ruling: English reverses former/latter mapping of stone vs wrappings

problems.quote: as the paralytic displayed his mat
problems.why: Missing verb: the paralytic 'carried' or 'bore' his mat; 'displayed' adds meaning not in source.
problems.fix: as the paralytic his mat
problems.ruling: Adds verb ‘displayed’ not in source, changes action

problems.quote: the hair was being planted again
problems.why: ἀντεφυτεύοντο is 'were being planted in return/restored,' but 'planted again' suggests regrowth; it's more 'set back in place/restored.'
problems.fix: the hair was being restored
problems.ruling: ‘planted again’ suggests new growth, source means restored

edits.old: Hades, mourning from below, was sending Lazarus onward.
edits.new: Hades, cut off from below, was sending Lazarus onward.

edits.old: he was arranging everything wisely as strategy for their benefit when he said to the Jews
edits.new: he was arranging everything wisely, as I said before, as strategy for advantage when he said to the Jews

edits.old: the one who lay dead with him
edits.new: the one sleeping in his presence

edits.old: was being remolded, its own into its own.
edits.new: was being remolded, the soul into its own body.

edits.old: preserve the former as a gift, keep the latter as witnesses.
edits.new: preserve the stone as a blessing, keep the burial wrappings as witnesses.

edits.old: as the paralytic displayed his mat.
edits.new: as the paralytic carried his mat.

edits.old: the hair was being planted again
edits.new: the hair was being restored

fixed: Hades, mourning from below: source κοπτόμενος means 'being struck/cut off,' not mourning; changed to 'cut off from below.'

he was arranging everything wisely as strategy for their benefit: source πρὸς λυσιτέλειαν means 'for advantage/profit,' not 'for their benefit'; changed to 'as strategy for advantage' and restored 'as I said before.'
the one who lay dead with him: source παρ' αὐτῷ καθεύδοντα means 'the one sleeping in his presence,' not 'dead with him'; changed to 'the one sleeping in his presence.'
its own into its own: source τὸ ἴδιον εἰς τὸ ἴδιον refers to the soul being remolded into its own body; changed to 'the soul into its own body.'

preserve the former as a gift, keep the latter as witnesses: source τὸ μὲν...τὸ δὲ refers to the stone and the burial wrappings respectively; changed to 'preserve the stone as a blessing, keep the burial wrappings as witnesses.'
as the paralytic displayed his mat: source κράβαττον implies carrying/bearing, not displaying; changed to 'as the paralytic carried his mat.'
the hair was being planted again: source ἀντεφυτεύοντο means 'were being restored/set back in place,' not 'planted again'; changed to 'the hair was being restored.'

problems.quote: burial wrappings
problems.why: Four different terms for same grave-clothes confuse reader into thinking they're distinct items.
problems.fix: Use one consistent term: 'burial cloths' or 'grave-bands'.

problems.quote: monument
problems.why: Reader may think 'monument' is a separate structure, not the tomb.
problems.fix: Use 'tomb' consistently.

problems.quote: But as I said before, he was arranging everything wisely, as I said before, as strategy for advantage when he said to the Jews
problems.why: Repetition and awkward embedding create incoherent syntax; 'as strategy for advantage' is opaque.
problems.fix: Revise: 'But as I said, he was wisely arranging everything as strategic advantage when he said'.

problems.quote: With a single-sound voice he woke the one sleeping in his presence
problems.why: 'Single-sound voice' is not English; presumably means 'single word' or 'one brief command'.
problems.fix: Use 'with a single word' or 'with one brief command'.

problems.quote: Hades, cut off from below, was sending Lazarus onward
problems.why: Metaphor is unclear: who/what is 'cut off'? Hades? Lazarus? 'Sending onward' to where?
problems.fix: Clarify: 'Hades, its power cut off, released Lazarus' or similar.

problems.quote: preserve the stone as a blessing
problems.why: Stone as 'blessing' is unexplained; seems opposite of its function as witness/proof.
problems.fix: Possibly 'preserve the stone as a monument' or check Greek for 'blessing' vs 'memorial'.

problems.quote: burial bands
problems.why: Three different terms for the same grave-clothes in one paragraph.
problems.fix: Use one term consistently, e.g. 'burial wrappings' throughout.

problems.quote: Before I go down, come out; in you is the pledge, but in me is the perfect thing.
problems.why: 'Before I go down' and 'the perfect thing' are obscure without context.
problems.fix: Render: 'Before I descend to Hades, come out; in you is the pledge of resurrection, in me its fulfillment.'

problems.quote: Hades, cut off from below, was sending Lazarus onward.
problems.why: 'Cut off from below' is an odd phrase; likely means Hades was compelled to release Lazarus.
problems.fix: Render: 'Hades, forced from below, was sending Lazarus up.'

fixed: Removed the repeated 'as I said before' from the opening sentence; the source has καθὼς προεῖπον once.
Changed 'single-sound voice' to 'single word' to match μονοφθόγγῳ φωνῇ, which means a single utterance or word.
Changed 'cut off from below' to 'forced from below' and 'onward' to 'up' to clarify that Hades was compelled to release Lazarus; the source has κοπτόμενος, meaning struck or forced.
Expanded 'Before I go down' to 'Before I descend to Hades' and clarified 'the perfect thing' as 'its fulfillment' to make the pledge/fulfillment contrast clear; the source has τὸ τέλειον.
Changed 'preserve the stone as a blessing' to 'preserve the one as a blessing' to match the source's τὸ μὲν...τὸ δὲ, which refers to the stone and the burial wrappings, not the stone alone.
Changed 'burial bands' back to 'burial cloths' to use one consistent term for κηρίαις and νεκροτάφια.

dismissed.quote: the soul into its own body
dismissed.why: τὸ ἴδιον εἰς τὸ ἴδιον means 'its own into its own,' not specifying 'soul into body'
dismissed.note: Spelling out 'its own into its own' as soul into body is a fair clarification of the reuniting image.

dismissed.quote: his feet and his face with burial bands
dismissed.why: κηρίαις means honeycomb/wax wrappings, not generic 'burial bands'; specific term for face wrappings
dismissed.note: κηρίαι/κειρίαι are the grave bands of John 11:44, not honeycomb; 'burial bands' is correct.

dismissed.quote: so that from the corpse-bearing stench itself they might learn that he had decayed and was not stolen.
dismissed.why: Greek says he was taken away (ἐσάπη) and not stolen, not that he decayed.
dismissed.note: ἐσάπη comes from σήπω, 'to rot', so 'decayed' is correct and plays on ἐκλάπη ('stolen').
